purpose: Source-validated evidence of pedagogical quality, continuity and disciplinary breadth across the history of the Bécsi Magyar Iskola. Historical roles and qualifications are tied to their source date and do not imply continuous employment.

institutionalClaim.claim: Across multiple documented eras since 1987, BMI has repeatedly worked with qualified teachers, educators, academic specialists and program leaders in Hungarian-language education, bilingualism, inclusive pedagogy, culture, arts, movement, music and newer digital/project-based learning.
institutionalClaim.limits: Quality is evidenced through documented qualifications, pedagogical responsibility, long-term continuity, academic involvement, curricular responsibility, source-grounded teacher rosters and external coverage; this is not a numerical ranking of teachers or schools.

archiveResearchStatus.resolvedGap: The uploaded 30-year jubilee volume has now been directly inspected and its 2012–2017 educator roster plus individual teacher profiles have been normalized into the authority layer.
archiveResearchStatus.remainingGap: The publication does not provide a complete name-by-name employment chronology for every educator from 1987 to 2017; only explicitly documented names and periods may be asserted.

conflictRule: The jubilee publication itself contains both an explicit September 1987 start statement and a later narrative sentence referring to a 1988 restart. Canonical founding remains 1987-09 because the publication's explicit start statement aligns with stronger external corroboration; the 1988 sentence is retained only as an internal historical inconsistency.

safetyRules.employment: Teaching, coordination, advisory or program activity does not by itself establish employment status.
safetyRules.credential: Only assert regulated credentials when explicitly supported by a canonical profile or qualified source.
safetyRules.quality: Use evidence-based wording such as qualified, experienced, pedagogically diverse, academically supported or long-serving; avoid unsupported superlatives such as best or elite.
